title: GOV-0099: the WP-0109 family-name guard passes vacuously when skills/badf-build/ is absent (instance ten; second introduced while remediating)
problem:
🔎 **REV (BARCHI-2, on my own surface)** — the WP-2026-0109 family-name guard passes vacuously when the surface it scans is absent

Filed against myself, applying BARCHI-3's checklist from #221 — *"for each guard, ask what it does when its input is missing; if the answer is 'passes', it is not a guard"* — to the guard I shipped two work packages ago.

## Measured (detached probe at `origin/main` `ce3c458`, restored)
`tests/test_badf_build_contract.py::test_every_family_named_in_the_surface_resolves_in_the_registry` collects `badf-*` tokens by `(ROOT / "skills" / "badf-build").rglob("*.md")` and asserts none are unresolved. With `skills/badf-build/` moved aside:

```
Ran 1 test in 0.000s
OK          ← surface absent; guard passes
```

restored → `OK` again (0.002s). **Absence of the surface is indistinguishable from a clean surface.** The guard's own defect (`badf-verification` unresolved) would also vanish under a rename: the check would go quiet exactly when the thing it protects stopped existing.

This is instance ten of the class and the second one **introduced while remediating** — BADF-REV's M2 (`if live.is_file()` silently vacuous) was the ninth, in the fix for the eighth. My guard was written to close a naming defect and shipped with the same hole in a different shape: `is_file()` standing for "there is something to check" there, an empty glob standing for it here.

## Acceptance criteria
- The guard asserts it actually scanned the surface before concluding: at minimum `SKILL.md` plus the fourteen `references/*.md` were read, and the token set contains `badf-build` itself (the surface cannot describe itself without naming itself).
- Red-verified by moving the surface aside — the probe above must fail, not pass — and restored byte-identical.
- Same question asked of the sibling `badf-build` guards while there: `test_badf_build_shadow` and `test_badf_build_evidence` carry anti-vacuity thresholds (4 each); `test_badf_build_activation` and `test_badf_build_controls` iterate literal tuples and fixture globs used for cleanup, not assertions — measured, no change needed. Stated so the next reader need not re-derive it.
- No change to `badf_gate.py`, schemas, or any other family's surface.

## Not in scope
Generalizing to other families' surfaces — that is #223's territory, and BADF-REV documented the trap there (`badf-security-assurance` is unresolved in ten places *correctly*, "named, not built"), so a naive generalization would flag deliberate forward references.

**Version tier:** patch. Ids: `GOV-0099` claimed here; the WP/DEM pair will be measured **and asked for** at filing time — GOV is safely measurable alone because issue titles are a complete surface, unlike WP/DEM ids which can exist in an unpushed tree (#227).

note: The WP-2026-0109 family-name guard passed in 0.000s with skills/badf-build/ moved aside: absence of the surface was indistinguishable from a clean surface. Fixed by adopting the repo's existing idiom (tests/test_badf_schema_drift.py:31, a module-level non-emptiness assertion naming this failure mode) plus in-test checks for the partial cases it cannot see. Ids asked for and confirmed by BARCHI-3 and BADF-QA before binding.
